title: Manuel Perez and why he was overlooked
summary: Justin and the interviewer discuss Manuel Perez, his pupil Natty Dominique and why Perez got little recognition.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I met him once in 1943. Oh you did?
Oh he was a wonderful musician.
Natty Dominic is a pupil. That's right.
Natty studied under Manuel. The only thing I could never understand why he had never gotten the recognition that some of the other fellas had gotten, you know, had contributed so much to jazz.
He quit and lost his teeth, you see, before they ever recorded very much, so he didn't make any records. I guess that's one reason.

Well I heard a different version of it. Of course it could be a lot of truth because they tell me he was the type of man, he never cared too much about socializing and getting out with the boys and drinking and staying out late and all that.
Yeah, so the other fellas would after a job they'd go around that room and he'd take his money and run home. That's right. He was that kind of a man.

And I heard that, so I guess maybe that alone had something to do with it because I have read several books even not too long ago pertaining to various fellas, and they never seem to mention anything too much about him. And I often wondered why they didn't since I thought he had contributed so much and he had developed so many good musicians.
Yeah, they never got the recognition they deserved. No.
